Not a person's machine and not a Windows candidate build.
method: The Windows native foundations workflow built both binaries natively (cargo build --locked -p agentdocker, rustc 1.98.1 stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, debug profile) and ran scripts/windows_daemon_smoke.py, whose report is the run's windows-daemon-smoke artifact and is copied here. The smoke drives a private daemon on a home the daemon creates itself under the runner's temporary directory, captures every command through pipes as a script would (bounded: exit in time, pipes closed after exit), and asks each daemon it started to exit.

earlier_runs_on_this_branch.what: the daemon refused the smoke's pre-created home: 'state or ancestor belongs to an untrusted Windows principal' (an elevated runner's objects belong to the Administrators group; Access::State requires the user's SID); and 'agentdocker ping' died with 'thread main has overflowed its stack' (1 MiB Windows main thread against the CLI's parser and main future in a debug build)

earlier_runs_on_this_branch.head: b167ebef
earlier_runs_on_this_branch.what: the daemon refused a home it made under a directory Python's mkdtemp made: 'state is writable by another Windows principal'. This run's root_acl shows why: CPython's os.mkdir(mode=0o700) on Windows gives the directory an explicit DACL of SYSTEM, Administrators and OWNER RIGHTS (S-1-3-4), and the ACL check does not count OWNER RIGHTS as the (already validated) owner

earlier_runs_on_this_branch.head: 5251cf4e
earlier_runs_on_this_branch.what: the on-demand agentd inherited the CLI's captured stdout/stderr pipe (Windows children inherit every inheritable handle), so the capture never saw EOF; command::detach now makes the client's standard handles non-inheritable
